purpose: Modular animation direction and honest playback review across four Xonix theme families; templates only, no animation generated.

prompts.intent: Separate replaceable visual parts from simulation behavior.
reference_requirements: Actual asset references and current simulation/state API or its explicit proposed interface.
prompts.prompt: Inspect {{ASSET_SET}}, the actual {{STATE_INTERFACE}} and {{FAMILY_DIRECTION}}. Propose independently replaceable components for body, rotor/wing parts, shadow, active trail, capture effects, hit/respawn effects, terrain materials, UI transitions and sound cues. Give stable proposed IDs, source/parent assets, anchor, draw order, timing owner, available skin choices and fallback. Distinguish components that need separate art from parameters of an existing renderer; do not multiply files without a production reason. Each component reads authoritative velocity, direction, phase or events but cannot modify position, collider, movement speed, damage, input or fill logic. Identify unavailable signals as dependencies rather than inventing supported fields. Preserve the existing art and logical footprint when swapping a component. Describe a compact example where only the body changes while rotors, trail and feedback retain their identities. Deliver a dependency table and handoff brief, not runtime implementation or a claim that animation works.
prompts.example_request: Make the drone body, rotors and trail independently replaceable.

prompts.intent: Specify state priorities, cancellation, clocks and fallbacks.
reference_requirements: Current state/event interface and component map.
prompts.prompt: Using {{STATE_INTERFACE}}, {{COMPONENT_MAP}} and {{TIMING_DIRECTION}}, draft presentation states for idle, move, turn, slow, boost, hit, respawn, capture and victory where their signals exist. For each component/state specify trigger, loop or one-shot behavior, explicit time units, return state, priority, cancellation and reduced-motion fallback. Resolve simultaneous events per component: hit can replace cosmetic turning, respawn replaces stale hit effects, and capture feedback can coexist with locomotion. Follow the authoritative game phase for victory; never freeze movement because a decorative clip starts. Preserve facing at zero velocity and use elapsed simulation time for world motion, with a separate intentional UI clock for paused menus. Define restart cleanup and event deduplication without introducing simulation changes. Mark unsupported events or state fields as proposed dependencies outside valid runtime data. Deliver a state/transition table plus a small set of playback scenarios; it remains a plan until assembled and played.
prompts.example_request: Define what happens when hit, boost and capture overlap.

prompts.intent: Make the actual displayed FPV silhouette smaller and readable.
reference_requirements: Actual drone image, target on-screen size and existing anchor/collider reference.
prompts.prompt: Inspect {{SOURCE_DRONE}} and create a separate compact pixel-art body/keyframe concept guided by {{TARGET_PIXEL_ENVELOPE}} and {{ANCHOR_REFERENCE}}. Reduce the occupied silhouette of the displayed drone, not merely its canvas or surrounding transparent margin. Preserve the approved Ukrainian identity, facing convention and recognizable body shape; use no Z markings anywhere and no hostile insignia on Ukrainian parts. Keep rotor attachments, trail attachment and logical center consistent while treating rotors as independently replaceable components. The reference collider and movement behavior remain unchanged. Show enough negative space around the body that direction remains legible at actual game scale, and avoid broad blur that enlarges its apparent hit area. Preserve the source and record this as derived keyframe artwork. Use the built-in image-editing tool with the inspected reference. Measure actual output dimensions and occupied pixels afterward; an AI contact sheet cannot establish exact frame alignment, alpha or a working animation.
prompts.example_request: Make the on-board FPV drone visibly smaller without changing its movement or hitbox.

prompts.intent: Drive modular rotor and body reactions from read-only state.
reference_requirements: Source parts or component references, recorded velocity/direction states and actual preview capabilities.
prompts.prompt: Inspect {{DRONE_PARTS}}, {{VELOCITY_TRACE}} and {{PREVIEW_CAPABILITIES}}. Plan separate body, rotor and optional shadow motion for a small Ukrainian FPV avatar. Body facing follows meaningful direction; idle retains the last facing. Rotor phase and optional visual rate can respond to the supplied velocity or state, but do not change simulation speed, movement or collider size. Keep rotor envelopes compact enough that the intended on-board silhouette remains small. Define world-clock looping, pause/resume, turns, slow/boost visual changes, hit cancellation and reduced-motion alternatives that preserve state legibility. Use no Z markings anywhere; the avatar’s Ukrainian allegiance remains explicit. Do not imply operational aircraft modeling or add unrequested weapons. If the preview cannot bind separate parts or read velocity, mark that requirement unsupported rather than claiming a working rig. Deliver component/timing rules and exact playback checkpoints; assembled loops must actually be played before approval as finished animation.
prompts.example_request: Animate separate rotors and subtle body turns using the same recorded movement trace.

prompts.intent: Keep enemy domains readable through distinct animation silhouettes.
reference_requirements: Enemy art and a role/domain map identifying supported versus proposed behaviors.
prompts.prompt: Inspect {{ENEMY_REFERENCES}} and {{ROLE_DOMAIN_MAP}} before creating a separate {{FAMILY_STYLE}} keyframe study. Distinguish an open-field mover, a patrol on changing interior capture contours, an enemy crossing revealed ground and a territory eroder. Give each a stable silhouette and restrained motion signature rather than identical glowing balls. Keep the fill-blocker mark attached only to roles the selected policy designates. Motion diagrams illustrate the declared domain; they do not implement homing, erosion, internal-contour traversal or new behavior. Preserve anchors, collider references and role identity across frames. Current FPV examples use explicit Ukrainian/hostile-military/neutral identity and no Z markings anywhere; Coupa uses process-friction objects rather than military motifs. Use the built-in image editor for the requested derivative and preserve all references. Record generated keyframes as concepts; timing, loop seams, interruption and actual-size readability require subsequent assembled playback.
prompts.example_request: Make the four enemy roles recognizable by silhouette and motion in every theme.

prompts.intent: Use material-specific Ukrainian motion without obscuring the arena.
reference_requirements: Specific chapter/tradition reference, actual asset set and recorded or explicitly proposed state trace.
prompts.prompt: Direct UKRAINE ATLAS animation using {{CHAPTER_REFERENCE}}, {{ASSET_SET}} and the fixed {{STATE_TRACE}}. Keep the chapter’s specific Ukrainian tradition coherent: a thread bird, painted charm, ceramic material or botanical accent can have its own restrained motion language without merging every tradition into one decoration. Separate avatar body/wing or ornament parts, live trail, local capture effect, terrain material and gallery/UI cues. Plan idle/move/turn, slow/boost, hit/respawn, capture and victory reactions only for supported signals, with priorities, cancel rules, explicit loop durations and reduced-motion alternatives. Compare microtile, detailed-object and hybrid appearance variants on exactly the same geometry and trace. Cultural motifs and people are not enemy identities; hazards stay abstract disruptions. Preserve the source art and medium, and keep live action above decorative motion. Deliver an authoring plan and playback checklist; a motion description does not produce or verify animated assets.
prompts.example_request: Give a Kosiv chapter restrained ceramic animation and three interchangeable appearance modes.

prompts.intent: Explore period-inspired motion with modern readability.
reference_requirements: Era/art direction, actual asset references and a fixed state trace.
prompts.prompt: Direct 1994 FOREVER animation from {{ERA_DIRECTION}}, {{ASSET_SET}} and {{STATE_TRACE}}. Choose a coherent period vocabulary such as limited-color DOS, console pixel clusters or a warm home-computer room; do not impose neon, CRT wobble or heavy bloom on every scene. Separate craft body, propeller/thruster visual parts, trail, local capture effects, terrain and UI. Preserve the same collider geometry and recorded movement across microtile, detailed-object and hybrid skins, retaining all three as available presentation choices. Specify idle/move/turn, supported slow/boost and hit/respawn responses, capture and victory as component-level states with loops, cancellation and clocks. Use economical keyframe changes and optional cosmetic accents while keeping a bright readable player/trail hierarchy. Reduced motion should replace busy effects with steady meaningful symbols. Sound cues can evoke a period instrument palette, but actual audio must be produced and listened to separately. Report unsupported preview features and do not call a storyboard working animation.
prompts.example_request: Compare a DOS-like motion style and a richer 16-bit style on the same level.

prompts.intent: Create clear business-world motion with modular brand art.
reference_requirements: Approved character/brand reference or explicit placeholder status, assets and fixed state trace.
prompts.prompt: Direct NAVI NETWORK motion from {{APPROVED_IDENTITY_REFERENCE}}, {{ASSET_SET}} and {{STATE_TRACE}}. If the identity reference is only a C-token placeholder, retain that status rather than claiming an exact official Navi mascot. Separate hero body/accent parts, connection trail, local savings-token effects, terrain/process materials, UI and sound cues. Use friendly restrained material motion and the approved palette; introduce no military imagery or nationality-coded enemies. Obstacles represent process friction, not customers or employees. Plan state-driven idle/move/turn, supported slow/boost, hit/respawn, capture and victory with clear priorities, cancellation, looping and reduced-motion fallbacks. Keep fictional game points separate from real customer claims. Provide microtile, detailed-object and hybrid variants using the same board geometry and trace. Cosmetic replacement never alters network objectives or collider data. Deliver a component/state plan and actual playback acceptance scenarios; no storyboard or generated clip proves a game runtime implements them.
prompts.example_request: Animate Navi’s connections and process obstacles without making it look like a military reskin.

prompts.intent: Keep microtile, detailed and hybrid terrain on identical geometry.
reference_requirements: Terrain semantics and an actual shared geometry fixture.
prompts.prompt: Using {{TERRAIN_ROLE_MAP}}, {{GEOMETRY_FIXTURE}} and {{FAMILY_PALETTE}}, plan three simultaneously available appearance variants: microtile material clusters, detailed object skins and a hybrid quiet grid with selected detailed objects. All three use identical tile coordinates, collision, traversal and capture behavior. Distinguish walls, player-only slow fields and player-lethal fields through material and shape, preserving the declared effects on enemies. Do not redefine a wall as damaging because its art looks sharp. Propose low-cost idle material motion and state-triggered accents only where supported; avoid distracting movement across every tile. Record animation bounds, loop timebase, cancellation on level reset and a steady reduced-motion version. Detailed object overhang must not hide corridors, player or active trail. Current FPV art keeps allegiance explicit and contains no Z markings. Deliver component/variant mappings and compare them in the same played fixture before claiming interchangeable animation is finished.
prompts.example_request: Support both microtiles and detailed terrain objects, plus a hybrid, without changing the board.

prompts.intent: Compose independent live-trail and local capture feedback.
reference_requirements: Actual capture events, style brief and supplied region geometry.
prompts.prompt: Design separate active-trail and capture-feedback components from {{CAPTURE_EVENT_INTERFACE}}, {{STYLE_DIRECTION}} and {{REGION_FIXTURE}}. The unfinished trail must remain visually distinct from settled boundaries and decorative lines inside artwork. On closure, use the authoritative captured region and event position for a local pulse or material reveal; never estimate capture geometry from generated pixels. A capture effect may coexist with locomotion and must not freeze movement, delay control or modify the fill result. Specify repeated-event handling, unique event identity, durations, priority, cancellation on restart/hit where appropriate and cleanup of lingering particles. Provide a reduced-motion immediate reveal with a quiet edge confirmation, and make audio cue timing a separately replaceable event mapping. Keep optional full-artwork victory presentation separate from normal region captures and actual captured percentage. Deliver keyframe/timing intentions and played-preview cases, reporting any unsupported event fields rather than inventing runtime support.
prompts.example_request: Make trail, closure pulse and capture sound replaceable independently.

prompts.intent: Make hit and recovery legible without inventing gameplay protection.
reference_requirements: Actual failure/respawn event semantics and avatar components.
prompts.prompt: Plan hit and respawn presentation using {{FAILURE_EVENT_INTERFACE}}, {{AVATAR_COMPONENTS}} and {{ACCESSIBILITY_DIRECTION}}. Use the authoritative collision position, failure reason and respawn state when supplied; do not infer a hit from sprite overlap or make animation apply damage. Define hit interruption of cosmetic turn/boost motion, cleanup of trails/effects after reset, and how actual respawn replaces stale hit visuals. Do not invent invulnerability, respawn delay or territory loss; those belong to the rules. Keep the player’s anchor and collider unchanged even when the visible silhouette briefly reacts. Prefer local outline/material cues over large flashes or disappearance that hides the avatar. Specify explicit one-shot durations, clock behavior during pause, cancellation, event deduplication and a reduced-motion alternative. Sound cues are independent and must not stack on repeated renders of one event. Deliver an event/state table and playback cases including hit during a turn and rapid restart; label unavailable events unverified.
prompts.example_request: Make failure clear and retries quick without changing the existing life-loss rules.

prompts.intent: Show the complete artwork while keeping score truth separate.
reference_requirements: Victory/phase interface, actual gallery artwork and family brief.
prompts.prompt: Plan a short victory-to-gallery sequence using {{VICTORY_EVENT_INTERFACE}}, {{GALLERY_ASSET}} and {{FAMILY_DIRECTION}}. Start only after the authoritative win event; freeze or dismiss active hazards according to the actual phase, then allow the complete artwork to be appreciated. Preserve actual captured fraction, time, lives and score as separate records; revealing the whole picture never changes an 80% result to 100% or alters the board’s collision data. Separate avatar gesture, local final-capture effect, gallery transition, UI navigation and sound cue so each can be replaced or skipped independently. Specify priority over ordinary motion, duration, cancellation/skip behavior, reduced motion and restart cleanup. Keep next-level and replay actions prompt and focusable. Do not require perfect mastery to grant the basic artwork reward unless the selected rules explicitly do so. Deliver a state/timing plan and actual playback checkpoints rather than claiming a static victory collage is an implemented flow.
prompts.example_request: Give each theme a satisfying skippable victory reveal while retaining honest completion stats.

prompts.intent: Cover keyboard, touch and controller UI motion states.
reference_requirements: Actual/proposed screen flow with status identified, separate UI assets and device targets.
prompts.prompt: Plan UI motion for {{SCREEN_FLOW}} using {{UI_ASSETS}} across {{DEVICE_TARGETS}}. Include focused/unfocused, pressed/released, selected, disabled, loading, empty/error, pause, retry, victory and gallery transitions where relevant. A focus effect must track actual keyboard/controller focus and never pretend that hover is focus on touch. Separate panel movement, selection marker, icon state, text resources and UI sound cues; real localized text remains outside generated art. Give each transition trigger, duration, priority, cancellation and a steady reduced-motion alternative. Use a deliberate UI clock only where the menu should continue during game pause. Opening/closing UI must not unexpectedly advance game simulation or steal a held movement input. Budget motion and visual footprint so controls remain usable on narrow screens; do not certify touch usability from a drawn phone. Provide a state table and an inspection sequence for rapid back/reopen and device/input changes, marking unsupported behavior as a proposal.
prompts.example_request: Design all focus, press, loading, pause and gallery animation states.

prompts.intent: Make sound cues replaceable and synchronized to real events.
reference_requirements: Actual event definitions and real audio inventory, including explicit missing assets.
prompts.prompt: Create a replaceable audio-cue map from {{EVENT_INTERFACE}}, {{SOUND_ASSET_INVENTORY}} and {{FAMILY_SOUND_DIRECTION}}. Separate continuous avatar/rotor ambience, live-trail tension, capture confirmation, pickup, hit, respawn, victory and UI cues. Trigger one-shots from actual events, with an explicit deduplication key so repeated rendered frames do not replay them. Record proposed offset, duration, overlap budget, priority, cancellation, fade and mute behavior. Continuous sound may read supplied velocity/state only if the audio route supports it; audio must never control movement or gameplay timing. Pause/resume follows the intended world/UI clock boundary. Different theme instruments can share the same event contract without sharing a military mood. Clearly distinguish existing inspected audio files, planned sound briefs and synthesized-but-unlistened outputs. Deliver a cue timeline and listening/playback checklist; do not invent a production tool or claim audio exists because the prompt names an instrument.
prompts.example_request: Let me swap every sound while preserving capture, hit and UI event timing.

prompts.intent: Set measurable motion budgets across devices and appearance modes.
reference_requirements: Actual display targets, rendered fixtures and component inventory.
prompts.prompt: Inspect {{DEVICE_TARGETS}}, {{ACTUAL_FIXTURES}} and {{COMPONENT_INVENTORY}} to propose responsive animation budgets. Measure occupied player/body/rotor pixels at the actual rendered size, not just canvas dimensions; for FPV compare the requested smaller silhouette with the fixed collider and trail anchor. Keep the same geometry/state trace across microtile, detailed-object and hybrid variants, with all three available as presentation options. Set clearly labeled proposed limits for texture sizes, visible effects, particle area/count, active decorative components, overdraw and simultaneous sound cues. Lower-cost tiers should simplify cosmetic motion while preserving warning meanings and gameplay timing. Record reduced-motion steady cues and how narrow-screen HUD placement avoids the playfield. Separate measured frame time/memory from estimates; a browser preview on one computer does not prove iPhone or Steam performance. Deliver a comparison table, missing-device coverage and a minimal next measurement plan; do not expand this into a new engine implementation.
prompts.example_request: Keep the drone small and the animation smooth on phones and larger screens.

prompts.intent: Require actual playback before claiming finished animation.
reference_requirements: Actual animation outputs, state contract and playable evidence rather than only contact sheets.
prompts.prompt: Review {{ANIMATION_OUTPUTS}} against {{STATE_CONTRACT}} and {{PREVIEW_EVIDENCE}}. Distinguish planned briefs, generated keyframes, assembled clips, played/reviewed animation and runtime-verified behavior. Inspect actual files for dimensions, real alpha, frame order, padding and pivots, then play the available clips to check loop seams, direction changes, state interruption, pause/resume and cleanup. Use the same trace for microtile, detailed-object and hybrid variants. Check the compact FPV occupied silhouette, trail attachment and allegiance/no-Z direction where applicable. Verify independent replacement of body, rotors, trail, effects, terrain, UI and sound cues only where the preview supports it. Inspect hit during turn, rapid captures, respawn, victory, reduced motion and repeated events without claiming unprovided scenarios. Sound requires actual listening evidence. A contact sheet or generated gameplay-looking video cannot prove runtime timing, collisions or input. Report concrete defects, tested scope and missing evidence; never advance readiness because an image looks polished.
prompts.example_request: Check which animations genuinely work and what still needs playback validation.
